 Hawaiʻi ranked No. 2 for lowest college costs relative to income 
 UH News » Academic News » Hawaiʻi ranked No. 2… 
 November 15, 2026 
 UH News 
 Reading time: 2 minutes 
 Higher education in Hawaiʻi is among the most affordable in the U.S., according to a national report released by personal-finance outlet WalletHub on November 12. Hawaiʻi ranked 47th out of 48 states analyzed—meaning it has the second-lowest higher education costs in the country when measured against household income.
 According to the study, States Where College Education Costs the Most & Least , college expenses in Hawaiʻi account for just 35.87% of median household income. WalletHub evaluated in-state undergraduate tuition, room and board, and additional college costs to calculate total affordability relative to local earning power. Nationwide, college costs have climbed approximately 26% over the last two decades, with the average national student loan balance approaching $44,000.
 “This independent report confirms what we at UH have long known: attending an in-state public institution offers incredible value and a clear path to debt-free graduation,” said UH President Wendy Hensel. “We remain deeply committed to keeping high-quality education accessible and affordable for local students.”
 Hawaiʻi borrowers carry less student debt than those in nearly every other state, earning the state the nation’s second-lowest student debt ranking according to a September 2026 WalletHub report. Across the UH System, among 2024–25 graduates who started as first-time freshmen:
 94% of UH Community College graduates complete their credentials with zero student debt.
 67% of UH four-year university graduates earn their degrees with zero student debt.
 Hawaiʻi Promise
 A cornerstone of this affordability track record is the Hawaiʻi Promise scholarship , which removes financial barriers for qualified local UH Community College students by covering unmet direct costs—including tuition, fees and books—after other financial aid is applied. Combined with targeted institutional aid and campus work opportunities, Hawaiʻi students are able to bypass heavy loan burdens seen across much of the mainland.
 For this study, WalletHub evaluated full-time, in-state undergraduate campus attendance costs across 48 states, excluding Alaska and Wyoming due to data constraints. Figures were adjusted based on each state’s median annual income to establish the final rankings.
